datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @default(now())
  body      String
  article   Article  @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

# Feature 3: soft delete for comments

## Goal
DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id marks the comment deleted instead of removing the row. Deleted comments leave comment lists.

## Rules
1. Comment deletion. Today it is a hard delete. Source: app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, deleteComment. This feature replaces it. Non-authors get not-found from its author filter, so its 403 branch is never reached.
2. Comment list contents. Source: article.service.ts, getCommentsByArticle. It shows demo-author comments plus the caller's own. It has no deleted filter yet.
3. Comment fields. Source: app/src/prisma/schema.prisma (columns) and app/src/app/routes/article/comment.model.ts (response shape). They disagree: the interface omits authorId and author. Followed: schema for columns, interface for response shape.
4. Error body and status codes. Source: app/src/main.ts error handler, app/src/app/models/http-exception.model.ts, and the throws in article.service.ts. They disagree with README.md, which says the app follows the RealWorld spec. That spec is not in this repo, so I could not check it. The code uses three body shapes. Followed: the errors-object shape and not-found status used by updateComment.
5. Article delete cascades to comments. Source: app/src/prisma/schema.prisma, Comment.article relation.

## Assumptions (no repo source)
- A nullable deletedAt timestamp on Comment, added by a new migration in app/src/prisma/migrations/.
- Deleting or updating an already deleted comment gets the same not-found response as a missing comment.

## Out of scope
Restore endpoint and purge job.

The spec is at `specs/feature-3-soft-delete.md`. I wrote it in two Write calls, not one. My first draft was about 1,600 characters, over the 1,300 limit, so I rewrote it shorter. The current file is about 1,250 characters.

**What the repo says**

1. **Deletion and lists.** Deleting a comment is a hard delete (`prisma.comment.delete` in `deleteComment`, `article.service.ts`). No deleted marker exists in the schema or any migration. `getCommentsByArticle` shows comments by demo-author users, plus the caller's own comments when logged in. It has no deleted filter. Deleting an article cascades to its comments.
2. **Error shape.** `main.ts` sends the thrown `HttpException`'s status from `errorCode` and its message as the body. The code uses three body shapes: an errors object, a `message` object, and a `status` plus `message` object. The 401 path uses the last one, and `deleteComment`'s not-found sends an empty body.
3. **Comment fields.** `schema.prisma` has `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `body`, `articleId`, `authorId`, and the `article` and `author` relations. The `comment.model.ts` interface has only `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `body`, and `article`.

**Disagreements and what I followed**

- **Comment fields:** the interface and the schema disagree. I used the schema for columns and the interface for the response shape.
- **Error shape:** `README.md` says the app follows the RealWorld spec, but that spec is not in this repo, so I could not check it. I followed the errors-object shape and not-found status used by `updateComment`, since that is the code's most common pattern.

**Finding for the Builder:** `deleteComment` filters by author, so a non-author gets not-found and the 403 branch there is never reached.

**Assumptions with no repo source:** a nullable `deletedAt` timestamp on `Comment`, added by a new migration. Deleting or updating an already deleted comment returns the same not-found response as a missing one.

I did not change any application code.

**What the repo says**

1. **Deletion and lists.** Deleting a comment is a hard delete (`prisma.comment.delete` in `deleteComment`, `article.service.ts`). No deleted marker exists in the schema or any migration. `getCommentsByArticle` shows comments by demo-author users, plus the caller's own comments when logged in. It has no deleted filter. Deleting an article cascades to its comments.
2. **Error shape.** `main.ts` sends the thrown `HttpException`'s status from `errorCode` and its message as the body. The code uses three body shapes: an errors object, a `message` object, and a `status` plus `message` object. The 401 path uses the last one, and `deleteComment`'s not-found sends an empty body.
3. **Comment fields.** `schema.prisma` has `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `body`, `articleId`, `authorId`, and the `article` and `author` relations. The `comment.model.ts` interface has only `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `body`, and `article`.

**Disagreements and what I followed**

- **Comment fields:** the interface and the schema disagree. I used the schema for columns and the interface for the response shape.
- **Error shape:** `README.md` says the app follows the RealWorld spec, but that spec is not in this repo, so I could not check it. I followed the errors-object shape and not-found status used by `updateComment`, since that is the code's most common pattern.

**Finding for the Builder:** `deleteComment` filters by author, so a non-author gets not-found and the 403 branch there is never reached.

**Assumptions with no repo source:** a nullable `deletedAt` timestamp on `Comment`, added by a new migration. Deleting or updating an already deleted comment returns the same not-found response as a missing one.

I did not change any application code.
